title: Definition
text: $$\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)$$ is the x-coordinate of the point on the circle that lies $$\frac{2}{3} rds$$ of the way along the circumference corresponding to the angle measure $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$.\n##figure1.gif##

title: $$30-60-90$$ triangle
text: The absolute values of the coordinates of this angle are given by the legs of a triangle with angles of $$30$$, $$60$$, and $$90$$. The hypotenuse has length $$1$$. The x-coordinate length comes from the side adjacent to the 60-degree angle, which is $$\frac{1}{2}$$.\n##figure2.gif##

title: Coordinate
text: The point on the unit circle with angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}$$ in the third quadrant. Thus the x-coordinate must be negative, so it is $$\frac{-1}{2}$$.\n##figure3.gif##
